questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This tests the ability to implement a branchless, 64-bit rotate using masking and shifts—a fundamental low-level technique in performance-critical code.

## Key Concepts
- 64-bit masking with &63 to constrain the rotation range
- Branchless rotation via (n >> r) | (n << (64 - r))
- Edge-case handling for k=0 without conditional branches

## Code Example
```javascript
function rotateRight64(n, k) {
  const r = k & 63;
  return (n >>> r) | (n << ((64 - r) & 63));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you generalize to arbitrary word sizes (e.g., 32-bit or 128-bit)?
- What are the trade-offs between rotate left and rotate right operations?
- How would this implementation behave on architectures with native rotate instructions?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to pack multiple fields into a single word, a common task in serialization and network protocols. It emphasizes precise bit-width handling and avoiding branches.

## Key Concepts

- Bitwise masking
- Bit shifts
- Field packing into a 32-bit word

## Code Example

```javascript
function packHeader(version, flags, length) {
  return ((version & 0x0F) << 28) | ((flags & 0xFF) << 20) | (length & 0xFFFFF);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extract version, flags, and length from the header?
- How would you validate inputs to prevent overflow or sign issues in languages with signed integers?
